paper_title: Disentangling Sequencing-Evidence Loss and Lineage Shift in Risk-Aware Genomic Susceptibility Reporting for Escherichia coli
supported_findings: Antibiotic-specific validation reporting and false-susceptible rates
Variation in false-susceptible errors across held-out cohorts
Calibration did not improve reportability under the evaluated policy
not_yet_established: Coverage-dependent change in AMR classifier predictions
Improvement from a combined coverage- and lineage-aware policy
False-susceptible risk control under simultaneous depth and lineage shift
important_caveats: Held-out BioProject experiments were explored during development
The sequencing-depth marker experiment is a single-isolate pilot
Coverage measurements do not prove marker-detection failure
Repeated seeds and genomic regions are not independent isolates
The frozen test set must remain excluded until methods are finalized
